title: Release Eng: add cherry-pick helper for LTS backports (conflict detection + PR templates)
author: Devon Price
description: Context: As part of the Runtime LTS initiative, we need a low-risk, repeatable way to apply small, curated fixes from mainline onto an LTS release branch (e.g. runtime-1.18-lts) while keeping diffs minimal and auditability high. Today, backports are a mostly-manual process (cherry-pick locally, resolve conflicts, open PR, remember labels/notes), which has already caused missed steps in branch-cut dry runs and slowed down response for Sev1/Sec fixes. This PR introduces a helper script to automate: (1) selecting commits/PRs to backport, (2) cherry-picking onto an LTS branch, (3) detecting conflicts early, and (4) opening a backport PR with an LTS-specific template and required metadata. What’s included: - New script tools/release/lts_backport.py (Python) that wraps git + gh (GitHub CLI) to create an LTS backport PR. - Conflict detection: script attempts a clean cherry-pick in a throwaway worktree; if conflicts occur, it aborts and prints the conflicting files/hunks and the exact commands to reproduce locally. It also supports an optional --allow-conflicts mode for cases where we still want a WIP PR for visibility, but defaults to fail-fast. - PR creation with template: opens a PR against a configurable LTS base branch, with a standardized title, body sections (Risk, Test Plan, Perf Gate, Rollback Notes, Compatibility), and checkboxes aligned with LTS change management. - Labels + reviewers: applies labels (lts/backport, runtime, security when requested) and requests review from a default reviewer set configurable in .github/lts-backport.yml; also supports overrides via flags. - Provenance metadata: includes original PR number, original merge commit SHA, and cherry-pick commit SHAs in the PR body, plus a machine-readable footer so the release notes generator can later associate backport PRs with the upstream PR. - Safety rails: refuses to run with a dirty working tree; refuses to backport merge commits by default (can be overridden with --allow-merge-commit); validates that the target LTS branch exists on origin; ensures the created branch name is unique and deterministic. Usage examples: - Backport by upstream PR: python tools/release/lts_backport.py --lts-branch runtime-1.18-lts --pr 23341 - Backport by commit SHA: python tools/release/lts_backport.py --lts-branch runtime-1.18-lts --sha 7a1c9f0d - Security hotfix (adds security label + tighter template language): python tools/release/lts_backport.py --lts-branch runtime-1.18-lts --pr 23425 --security Notes on naming and semantics: - Backport branches are created as backport/runtime-1.18-lts/<upstream_ref>-<shortsha> (ex: backport/runtime-1.18-lts/pr-23341-7a1c9f0d). - PR title defaults to: [LTS runtime-1.18-lts] Backport <upstream_ref>: <upstream title> - PR body includes a ‘Backport Metadata’ footer used by tooling; please do not edit that section manually. Non-goals: This script does not decide backport eligibility; it’s an execution tool only. The rubric/approvals remain in the LTS policy docs and enforced in review + CI gates. It also does not attempt to auto-resolve conflicts. Follow-ups: - ENG-4824 will wire this into release-manager checklists and CI workflows. - ENG-4826 will ingest the backport metadata footer when generating LTS release notes. - We should consider adding a ‘dry-run’ mode that skips branch push/PR creation once we finalize the template language with Product/Support.
commits: tools/release: add lts_backport helper script (git/gh wrapper)
tools/release: add backport PR template + metadata footer format
docs: document LTS backport workflow and required flags
tests: add unit tests for parsing upstream refs and branch naming
review_conversation: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng): The direction is right. Two asks before merge: (1) default reviewers should include at least one Runtime lead + Release Eng lead, and (2) the PR body should include a dedicated section for perf validation (even if it’s ‘N/A’), since perf regressions are a hard blocker for enterprise. Devon Price (author): Updated .github/lts-backport.yml defaults to include Connor + Samir; added a ‘Perf gate’ section to the template with required link or explicit ‘not run’ justification. Sahana Iyer (CI/Build): Please don’t rely on a globally-installed gh; our release containers have it but some dev laptops don’t. Can we emit a clearer error + install instructions? Also can we avoid requiring write access if someone just wants conflict detection? Devon Price: Added preflight checks: if gh is missing, we print a single-line install hint and exit non-zero. Added --local-only mode that runs the worktree cherry-pick + conflict detection without pushing or opening a PR. Samir Qureshi (Runtime): The ‘refuse merge commits’ default is good. Can we also block ‘cherry-pick a PR merge commit’ by default (those often pull in extra unrelated commits)? Devon Price: Script now resolves PR -> merge commit -> first parent by default; you can override with --use-merge-commit. Also prints the upstream commit list in the PR body so reviewers can sanity check scope. Kira Volkov (tooling): Minor: branch name can exceed Git ref limits if upstream title is used. Looks like you’re only using pr-number/sha; good. Please add unit test for branch naming collisions. Devon Price: Added test case for deterministic suffix and collision retry (adds -2, -3...). Connor O’Brien: Looks good; approved. CI note: first run failed due to missing mypy stubs in the test image; rerun after pinning types-requests in dev requirements passed.
release_notes: Internal tooling: add lts_backport helper script to standardize cherry-picks and backport PR creation for runtime LTS branches.
